brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Three hex bases in a tight triangle: full base at (0,0,0), full base at (0,1,0), and a west-half base at (1,0,0). Joint bolts on the joints lock them (LOOSE_BODY cleared). check_build: ok, meshClash clear.
Slide drawer drawer:0#1,0#cut on the cut face of the half base at (1,0,0), key e. Required the west half base; the east half had no drawer socket.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at the junction of cells (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0), the only three-cell junction in the build. A plain solid spike was refused for platforms, so I used the mount variant.

setSpikeAccessory platform-sm was accepted on the mount spike (no error), but the build listing does not show the accessory, so I could not independently confirm it is attached. Verify visually before relying on it.

finish.summary: Built a compact three-base desk unit: two full bases and a west-half base forming a triangle, with a slide drawer on the half base's cut face, joint bolts locking the joints, and a mount spike at the three-cell corner carrying a small platform. check_build reports no rule errors and a clear mesh check. The platform's attachment is accepted but not visible in the build listing.

M6 x 16 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
